Algebra 1 | Quarter 2 | Unit 3: Linear Relationships

Is the Climb Steady?

Spotting a constant rate of change

Duration
50 minutes
Grade level
Grades 8–9
Topic
Linear Relationships
Standards
8.F.A.3, 8.F.B.4, HSF-LE.A.1

Students recognise a constant rate of change in tables, graphs, equations and situations, and decide whether a relationship is linear.

  2. 3Essential question
  3. 4Mathematical foundation

2Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson, students will be able to:

  • Decide whether a table shows a linear relationship by checking for a constant rate of change.
  • Find the rate of change from a table, including tables with unequal steps in x.
  • Connect a linear relationship’s table, graph, equation and verbal description.
  • Explain why some real relationships are not linear.

3Essential question

How can you tell, from just a few numbers, whether a climb has a steady grade?

5MTB connection

Fire roads are often built at a steady grade, so each 100 ft of road gains the same elevation: a linear relationship. Singletrack changes grade constantly, so its profile curves.

A rider who knows the climb is linear can predict exactly how much elevation is left from any point. That’s a real pacing tool.

The mathOn the trail
Constant rate of changeA steady-grade fire road
First differencesElevation gained per equal stretch of trail
Non-linearA trail that steepens or eases
y = mx + bElevation = grade × distance + start elevation
